# Solar on Our Roof

One year of data from 24 panels

Residents' meeting, February 2026

<!-- Thank the roof committee by name: Ana, Piotr and Leila. Remind everyone that the numbers come from the inverter log, they are not estimates. -->

---

## Why we did it

- Electricity for the shared areas cost **€3,900** in 2023
- The flat roof was empty and gets sun from 9 am to 5 pm
- A municipal grant covered 30% of the installation
- Six neighbours had asked for it at two meetings in a row

---

![bg right:40%](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

## The system

- 24 panels of 410 W: **9.84 kWp**
- One 8 kW inverter in the bike room
- No battery (yet)
- Installed in three days, March 2025
- Monitored from a web dashboard

---

## Production by season

| Season   | Produced (kWh) | Used in the building | Sold to the grid |
| :------- | -------------: | -------------------: | ---------------: |
| Spring   |          3,480 |                  41% |              59% |
| Summer   |          4,620 |                  36% |              64% |
| Autumn   |          2,310 |                  58% |              42% |
| Winter   |          1,190 |                  83% |              17% |
| **Year** |     **11,600** |              **47%** |          **53%** |

<!-- Winter is the surprise here: almost everything we produce is used on the spot, because the lift and the heating pumps run all day. -->

---

## What surprised us

1. **Pigeons.** Nesting under the panels cut output by 6% until we fitted mesh.
2. **The lift is the big consumer.** It uses more than all the corridor lighting together.
3. **Summer surplus is cheap.** We sell at €0.07 and buy at €0.24, so
   - using power at midday matters more than producing more
   - the laundry room timer now runs from 11 am to 3 pm

---

## Payback

# 6.5 years

> Cost after the grant: €10,400. Savings and sales in the first year: €1,610.

The panels are guaranteed for 25 years.

<!-- 10,400 divided by 1,610 is about 6.5. If prices keep rising it will be shorter, but do not promise that. -->

---

## What we propose for 2026

- Add a **10 kWh battery** to use the summer surplus in the evening
- Move the two car chargers to solar-first mode
- Share the dashboard with every flat

**Vote at the March meeting.** Questions: roof@orchardlane.example
